h: Hyperpigmentation, ACTH over 1000, bitemporal hemianopia after bilateral adrenalectomy: diagnosis?
d: Ectopic ACTH from small cell lung cancer
p: Removing the adrenals for Cushing disease removes cortisol feedback, so the pituitary adenoma grows, causing visual field loss and high ACTH/MSH pigmentation. Treat with pituitary surgery or radiation.
CA-125 is raised in epithelial ovarian cancer (used for monitoring); CA 19-9 marks pancreatic cancer and AFP marks yolk sac tumor and HCC.
Phenytoin: gingival hyperplasia, hirsutism, nystagmus, megaloblastic anemia, teratogenic fetal hydantoin syndrome, and CYP450 induction.

h: Early pregnancy: supplement that prevents neural tube defects?
p: Give folic acid (400 micrograms daily, higher with prior NTD or antiepileptics) before conception and in early pregnancy; high-dose vitamin A is teratogenic.

h: Which vitamin D form requires UV light for its synthesis in skin?
p: UVB converts 7-dehydrocholesterol to cholecalciferol, which is hydroxylated in liver (25-OH) then kidney (1,25-OH, calcitriol). Ergocalciferol is the plant-derived form.

h: Earliest nuclear sign of irreversible cell injury?
p: Necrotic nuclei progress from pyknosis (shrunken, basophilic) to karyorrhexis (fragmentation) to karyolysis (dissolution).

h: Adult nephrotic syndrome with subepithelial deposits and thick GBM: antibody target?
p: Membranous nephropathy: anti-PLA2R IgG, spike-and-dome appearance, linked to hepatitis B, lupus, malignancy and NSAIDs. Minimal change shows foot process effacement only.

h: RA drug with greatest risk in alcoholic liver disease?
p: Methotrexate is hepatotoxic (fibrosis, cirrhosis) and contraindicated with significant liver disease or heavy alcohol use; give folic acid and monitor LFTs.

h: Impetigo with elevated anti-DNase B: later complication?
p: Skin infection with nephritogenic group A strep can cause PSGN 2-3 weeks later; rheumatic fever follows pharyngitis only, not skin infection.

h: Recurrent mild jaundice with isolated unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia: diagnosis?
p: Gilbert syndrome: mildly decreased UGT1A1 activity, jaundice with fasting, stress or illness, benign and needs no treatment.

h: Bilateral thalamic hemorrhage: which sensory modality is spared?
p: All senses relay through the thalamus except olfaction, which reaches the cortex directly via the olfactory tract (piriform cortex).
Glucagon raises blood glucose via glycogenolysis, gluconeogenesis, lipolysis and ketogenesis. Glucagonomas cause necrolytic migratory erythema, diabetes and weight loss.

h: Detecting a DNA-binding protein with a labeled DNA probe: technique?
p: Southern detects DNA, Northern RNA, Western protein with antibody, and Southwestern detects DNA-binding proteins with a DNA probe.

h: Allergic asthma bronchoconstriction: which mediators drive it?
p: Leukotrienes C4, D4 and E4 cause potent, prolonged bronchoconstriction in asthma; montelukast blocks the CysLT1 receptor, zileuton blocks 5-lipoxygenase.

h: Tricuspid regurgitation murmur louder on inspiration: why?
p: Inspiration increases venous return to the right heart and RV stroke volume, intensifying right-sided murmurs (Carvallo sign); left-sided murmurs soften.

h: Lateral thigh pain with reduced patellar reflex: herniated disc level?
p: L4 root: knee jerk diminished and weak quadriceps; L5 gives foot drop; S1 diminishes the Achilles reflex.

h: Radiolucent stone in a leukemia patient on chemotherapy: composition?
p: Tumor lysis raises uric acid and low urine pH favors uric acid stones, which are radiolucent; treat with hydration, alkalinization and allopurinol or rasburicase.
Vasospastic digital ischemia triggered by cold or stress; use dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers, avoid beta-blockers and vasoconstrictors.
